_note: JSON sidecar for migration-manifest.yaml. The wizard runtime CLI consumes JSON; YAML is the human-facing companion. Both files MUST stay in sync.

artifact_notes.agents/lib/external_write/_ext_write_sta: New helper that decides, in plain language, what to say about ONE blocking item on the shared migration queue: a real writer bypass keeps the familiar "rebuild it" wording, but anything else recorded on the same queue -- for example, a safety check that itself could not finish -- is described in its own words instead, so guidance never tells you to rebuild a file that was never the problem.
artifact_notes.agents/lib/external_write/capability_hea: The health check's bypass-writer report now carries a ready-to-relay, plain-language sentence for each flagged item, so a genuinely different kind of problem is never described with the bypass writer's rebuild wording. What blocks is unchanged.
artifact_notes.agents/lib/external_write/capability_run: When a capability cannot yet look at the outside system in read-only mode, the refusal now names the exact adapter that needs a read-only reader added to it, and says plainly that rebuilding the capability will not fix this -- instead of telling you to rebuild the capability, which sent you in a circle.
artifact_notes.agents/lib/external_write/operator_accep: Turning a capability on now describes each blocking item accurately: a real bypass writer still gets the familiar rebuild-it guidance, but any other kind of blocking item recorded on the same shared queue is described in its own words, so you are never told to rebuild something that was never the writer at fault.

migrations.migration_steps: 1. Run the update check (it reports what's new + the recommendation). 2. On the operator's yes, the assistant applies it ("${{WIZARD_HOME:-$HOME/agent-wizard}}/scripts/wizard" self-upgrade --to v0.21.0 --apply). 3. A backup is taken first; the operator's own data, rules, credentials, and logs are never touched.
migrations.notes: Minor-additive release to v0.21.0 (Cut 1.7). When a capability cannot yet look at the outside system in read-only mode, the refusal now names the exact adapter that needs a read-only reader added to it, and says plainly that rebuilding the capability will not fix this -- previously it told the operator to rebuild the capability itself, which sent them in a circle chasing a file that was never the problem. The health check and turning a capability on also now describe each blocking item in its own accurate words: a real bypass writer keeps the familiar rebuild-it guidance, but a different kind of blocking fact recorded on the same shared queue (for example, a safety check that itself could not finish) is described honestly instead, in wording that does not name a fix that does not apply to it. Nothing about what blocks changed -- only what is said about it. This release also closes a gap in the update tool itself: every upgrade and safety review now actually checks and durably records whether each capability's read-only path is present, closing a gap where that check could silently be skipped without anyone knowing. No breaking changes; all existing capabilities and files are unaffected.
migrations.preflight: Verify the operator project carries a .wizard/manifest.json whose foundation_bundle_version is v0.20.0 (or any version in the supported range). A backup is taken automatically.
migrations.rollback: Restore from .wizard/backups/pre-v0.21.0/ and set foundation_bundle_version back to v0.20.0.

On the operator's yes, the assistant applies it ("${{WIZARD_HOME:-$HOME/agent-wizard}}/scripts/wizard" self-upgrade --to v0.21.0 --apply). 3. A backup is taken first; the operator's own data, rules, credentials, and logs are never touched.
migrations.notes: Minor-additive release to v0.21.0 (Cut 1.7). When a capability cannot yet look at the outside system in read-only mode, the refusal now names the exact adapter that needs a read-only reader added to it, and says plainly that rebuilding the capability will not fix this -- previously it told the operator to rebuild the capability itself, which sent them in a circle chasing a file that was never the problem. The health check and turning a capability on also now describe each blocking item in its own accurate words: a real bypass writer keeps the familiar rebuild-it guidance, but a different kind of blocking fact recorded on the same shared queue (for example, a safety check that itself could not finish) is described honestly instead, in wording that does not name a fix that does not apply to it. Nothing about what blocks changed -- only what is said about it. This release also closes a gap in the update tool itself: every upgrade and safety review now actually checks and durably records whether each capability's read-only path is present, closing a gap where that check could silently be skipped without anyone knowing. No breaking changes; all existing capabilities and files are unaffected.
migrations.preflight: Verify the operator project carries a .wizard/manifest.json whose foundation_bundle_version is v0.6.9 (or any version in the supported range). A backup is taken automatically.
